name: Child-size protective earmuffs
blurb: Compare fit, the stated noise reduction rating, and instructions for the activity. Check the seal around glasses or a hat.
useCase: When appropriately fitted hearing protection is needed
alternative: Ask whether the venue lends suitable hearing protectors; a quieter activity may fit better.

name: A comfortable brimmed hat
blurb: Let your child try the fabric, fastening, and brim. Check that it does not obstruct their view or interfere with other equipment.
useCase: An optional way to manage overhead light
alternative: Start with a familiar hat or choose a shaded break location.

name: A familiar hand-held fidget
blurb: Check the actual sound, texture, age label, and detachable parts. Choose something your child already wants to use.
useCase: Something to do with hands during a wait
alternative: Bring a suitable toy already used at home instead of buying a multipack.

name: A small communication card
blurb: Use familiar symbols or words for requests such as help, break, bathroom, and finished. Keep existing communication tools available.
useCase: Sharing a practical request during an outing
alternative: Make a paper card with your child; a purchased set is optional.

name: An optional visual timer
blurb: Check whether the timer ticks, flashes, or sounds an alarm and whether those features can be turned off. Offer it only if your child finds it useful.
useCase: Showing a known interval, such as a planned break
alternative: Use a paper sequence or a familiar phone display; avoid promising a countdown for an uncertain queue.

name: An easy-to-open outing bag
blurb: Check its weight when filled, the venue's bag rules, and whether essential items can be reached without unpacking everything.
alternative: Use a bag you already own and keep a short packing list inside.

name: Comfortable familiar clothes
blurb: Check seams, labels, fastenings, weather suitability, and ease of changing. A clothing label cannot tell you whether your child will like the feel.
useCase: A comfortable outfit or spare change for a trip
alternative: Choose an already-familiar outfit before buying anything described as sensory clothing.
